title: First aid step cards
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y11 lesson 3 (First aid step cards (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 3: First aid: CPR on a cushion and the recovery position. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Step
Detail
rows: Speaker on; send someone for an AED
Switch on and follow the voice

bullets: Centre of the chest, heel of hand
30 compressions : 2 rescue breaths, or hands-only CPR

panels.title: Recovery position
points: On their side, head tilted back

cards: Call 999 on speaker; send someone for an AED
Switch on the AED and follow its voice
30 chest compressions: 5 to 6 cm, 100 to 120 a minute
Open the airway: head tilt, chin lift
Check for a response: shout and tap the shoulders
2 rescue breaths if trained, or hands-only CPR
Check breathing for up to 10 seconds
blocks.task: put them in order for an unresponsive casualty who is not breathing normally.
blocks.answer: 1 Check for danger; 2 Check for a response: shout and tap the shoulders; 3 Shout for help; 4 Open the airway: head tilt, chin lift; 5 Check breathing for up to 10 seconds; 6 Call 999 on speaker; send someone for an AED; 7 30 chest compressions: 5 to 6 cm, 100 to 120 a minute; 8 2 rescue breaths if trained, or hands-only CPR; 9 Switch on the AED and follow its voice. If they are breathing normally: recovery position, call 999 and keep checking their breathing.

keywords.def: cardiopulmonary resuscitation: chest compressions (and rescue breaths) to keep blood moving
automated external defibrillator: a device that can restart the heart
a safe position for an unresponsive person who is breathing
DRABC: danger, response, airway, breathing, call for help

questions.q: Practise 30 compressions on a cushion with the teacher's count (100 to 120 a minute).
questions.a: Rhythm kept at about two per second.

questions.q: Core: Sequence cards (pupil PDF): put the steps for an unresponsive casualty in order and say what changes if they are breathing.
questions.a: Danger, response, airway, breathing, 999, CPR and AED; breathing: recovery position.

questions.q: Extend: Find where the nearest public AED is to your home (with a parent, using The Circuit or a local map).
Stretch: In the portal response box, explain why hands-only CPR is still worth doing. Start: 'Hands-only CPR...'
questions.a: Hands-only CPR keeps blood with oxygen moving to the brain until help arrives.

questions.q: An adult is unresponsive and not breathing normally. After calling 999 you should...
options: Put them in the recovery position
questions.a: B) Start CPR. No normal breathing means CPR; the recovery position is for someone who is breathing.

questions.q: CPR compression rate? A) 30 a minute B) 100 to 120 a minute C) 200 a minute
Big question: if it happened at home, what would you do first?
questions.a: Check danger and response, call 999, start CPR, get an AED.
